newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: S.Africa's Mandela urges economic partnerships.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mandela urges economic partnerships.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela on Monday urged business, labour and non-governmental organisations to form partnerships with governments in southern Africa to build economic development in the region.

Saying the governments of the 12-member Southern African Development Community (SADC) had no illusions about the immensity of the challenge, Mandela added that the contribution of particularly the private sector was critical.
"Development will not be achieved if it is regarded as the responsibility only of government," he told a business conference in Kasane, Botswana.
"We should join in a partnership to make development integral to private sector activities, rather than some extra contribution which the private sector might or might not chose to engage in."

Mandela said confidence could nevertheless be drawn from the SADC's determination to work for increased economic integration to achieve greater prosperity in the region, and the political stability which underpinned this move.
"A joint approach to regional infrastructure has become a reality. The development corridors now being promoted...can help change the economic face of the region," he added.

Seated at a central table with Botswana President Ketumile Masire, Uganda's Yoweri Museveni, Tanzania's Benjamin Mkapa, Ghana's Jerry Rawlings and Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Bin Mohamad, Mandela said that no nation could prosper in isolation.

"In a period defined by growing interdependence of nations and the emergence of regional blocs in a global economy, we need a regional framework for development and a collective voice to be heard in the economic forums of the world," he said.
"It is vital that the potential of our region should be given maximum exposure to the international business community."

The conference was attended by the SADC member states of Angola, Botswana, Lesotho, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Swaziland, Tanzania, Zambia, Zimbabwe, as well as Uganda and Ghana.
